title: The Last Clap at Our Wedding
rule: The town cloud rains over the source of the most recent clap.
loophole: A quiet wooden clap beats a crowd if it comes later.
cost: Pip spends the umbrella takings to bring the irrigation tank to Nell. Nell chooses a soaked wedding dress.

cast.want: Give Nell the weather she has provided for thirty other brides.
Hear the applause her late mother promised her.
Save his seedlings and carry his wife’s promise into the ceremony.
Marry Nell and keep her dry without missing the bouquet toss.
Give her niece a proper round of applause.
Deliver a wedding cake that people can still slice.
Put on the town’s loudest ovation.
Back the bandleader and watch the wedding.

beats.line: In Ovation, applause brings rain. At my sister's wedding rehearsal, Aunt Vi clapped over the cake. The baker handed out straws.
beats.visible: Vi claps by the tiered cake. The rain column crosses the fair; Sol catches the plate.

beats.line: Brides usually hire Nell to clap in a potato field. She's stood in the rain for thirty strangers. Today she was the bride.
beats.visible: Nell demonstrates the field job with rain overhead. Cut to her floral veil in company.

beats.line: I promised her a dry wedding. Dad wanted the rain too. His strawberry tank was empty. In that heat, the seedlings had one afternoon.
beats.visible: Pip sees the cart’s empty basin; Raf checks the low plants and shows him a handful.

beats.line: I booked a standing ovation at the nursery. Two trumpets, eight rows of hands, one man applauding with a fish. The cloud came running.
beats.visible: The band leads the ovation beside the cart. The cloud arrives over its opening.

beats.line: The band finished. Eighty pairs of hands went down. Then Nell came out. One tiny clap beside her elbow. The rain went straight down her dress.
beats.visible: Nell walks under the flower arch and carries the closed bouquet. Rain races away from the nursery toward her.

beats.line: I accused Gus. He held up both hands. They were in socks. He'd taken the dress code personally.
beats.visible: Gus slowly presents two raspberry mittens. Nell looks from one to the other.

beats.line: It clapped again. Nobody touched Nell. Except her bouquet, which had never expressed an opinion before.
beats.visible: Pip leans in; the flowers separate enough to reveal a pair of wooden fingers.

beats.line: Two little wooden hands. Mum used them to cheer from her hospital bed. Dad had glued a new spring in. There was still glue on his thumb.
beats.visible: Raf takes the mechanical flowers, opens the hands and shows Nell his thumb.

beats.line: He'd promised Nell she'd hear Mum's clap at her wedding. Now he was trying to snap the spring so she could stay dry. I caught his wrist.
beats.visible: Pip intercepts Raf’s raised hand before he can silence the spring. Nell sees the mechanism.

beats.line: Wait. Vi had beaten a whole choir with one clap. Maybe the cloud didn't care who was loudest. Maybe it only cared who was last.
beats.visible: Pip points to Vi at the cake, then back to the hands; the audience has seen both clues before.

beats.line: I tried one quiet clap by the tank. Rain. The flowers clicked on the other side of the yard. The cloud doubled back. Dad hadn't broken anything.
beats.visible: One cloud crosses between two simultaneously visible sources. It reverses only after the wooden hands meet.

beats.line: I could put the flowers beside the strawberries. Nell would get a dry wedding. She'd never hear the one person she'd been waiting for.
beats.visible: Pip starts toward the seedlings with the bouquet, looks back at Nell and deliberately stops.

beats.line: I gave her the flowers. Then I paid the band my whole summer's umbrella money to wheel Dad's tank across the square. If the cloud came to Nell, the tank could too.
beats.visible: Pip gives Nell the bouquet and pays the driver. The empty cart rolls under the wedding arch.

beats.line: 'Thirty weddings in a potato field,' Nell said, stepping into the tank. 'I think I'd like to get wet at mine.' Gus tucked the rings into a sock.
beats.visible: Nell steps into the open cart at the flower arch. Her bouquet rises above the rim. Gus looks down at his mitten.

beats.line: At 'I do,' Dad wound the spring. The wooden hands clapped for my sister. Everyone else danced with their hands in their pockets.
beats.visible: The wooden palms close. Rain arrives at Nell inside the tank; feet keep time around her.

beats.line: By the last dance the tank was full. Dad's strawberries had their summer. My sister had her clap. The baker served the cake in teacups.
beats.visible: Sol serves his soggy cake while the cart fills to its gold band. Raf and Nell dance either side of its rim.

beats.line: Then Nell tossed the bouquet. Gus caught it. Both socks filled up.
beats.visible: The bouquet arcs to Gus. His delighted grin changes as the rain column leaves Nell and lands on his mittens.
